GAMENIGHT / DOCUMENTATION

Bevy

gamenight-bevy is a Bevy plugin that does the GameNight side of a game for you. Add it next to DefaultPlugins, read GameNightEvent messages and ask GameNight for each seat's controller. The plugin:

  • connects when GameNight launched the game and runs standalone otherwise, with the keyboard and every local gamepad as seats, so your input code is the same in both modes;
  • follows Prepare, Start, Pause, Resume and Dispose, and sends Ready two frames after you call ready(), so the first frame of your level exists before Start;
  • keeps the window hidden and unfocused while warming, shows it borderless fullscreen on Start and Resume and hides it on Pause and Dispose;
  • pauses every playing AudioSink while you are not on the TV and updates at 10 fps while warm or paused, while still hearing Resume;
  • gives each seat its own controller by host token, with deadzones, press edges and a release required after Start and Resume;
  • reports activity so nobody is marked asleep, and rumbles a seat's pad;
  • re-declares your settings, phone buttons, phone screen and text commands after every reconnect, and replays setting changes from your own menu;
  • reports frame timing every ten seconds of play, with CPU, GPU, OS, memory and window size;
  • sends F1 to the party (physical Back is the host's own) and exits when the host goes away.

The demo game in sdk/bevy/demo, Star Catch, uses every feature on this page. Each excerpt below is read from it. CI runs it through the conformance harness against a real host on every push.

Add the plugin

The plugin targets Bevy 0.20 (Rust 1.97.1 or newer). Pin a reviewed commit of the public repository:

[dependencies]
bevy = "0.20"
gamenight-bevy = { git = "https://github.com/ontola/gamenight", rev = "YOUR_REVIEWED_COMMIT" }

Replace YOUR_REVIEWED_COMMIT with an actual commit hash.

Set up the app

Wrap your window in managed_window, so a game GameNight launched starts hidden and unfocused. A window that flashes up while warming steals the TV from the game being played. Run simulation systems only while gameplay_runs: that is what freezes play, timers and bots on Pause.

fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    App::new()
        .add_plugins(DefaultPlugins.set(WindowPlugin {
            primary_window: Some(managed_window(Window {
                title: TITLE.into(),
                resolution: (1280u32, 720u32).into(),
                ..default()
            })),
            ..default()
        }))
        .add_plugins(GameNightPlugin::new("bevy-demo"))
        .insert_resource(ClearColor(Color::srgb(0.06, 0.07, 0.13)))
        .insert_resource(Match {
            rules: Rules {
                round_seconds: args.round.unwrap_or(60),
                ..default()
            },
            ..default()
        })
        .insert_resource(args)
        .init_resource::<Menu>()
        .add_systems(Startup, (setup, declare))
        .add_systems(
            Update,
            (
                gamenight_events,
                standalone_start,
                menu_input,
                (steer, bots, physics, stars, bombs, round_clock)
                    .chain()
                    .run_if(gameplay_runs)
                    .run_if(menu_closed),
                (draw_hud, draw_menu, phone_updates, music_volume, shot),
            )
                .chain(),
        )
        .run();
}

Source: sdk/bevy/demo/src/main.rs

GameNightPlugin::new turns the window, audio and throttling on. Set manage_window, fullscreen, manage_audio, throttle_when_hidden or report_activity to false to handle one of them yourself.

Follow the session

Every message from GameNight arrives as a GameNightEvent. On Prepare, build the level for exactly the seats you were given, then call ready(). Opt into live roster changes with participation(true) first if new players can join mid-round, as here. Nothing restarts on RosterChanged or PlayersUpdated: newcomers get a pawn, leavers lose theirs, and a new name, colour or face is painted onto the same pawn.

fn gamenight_events(
    mut commands: Commands,
    mut gn: ResMut<GameNight>,
    mut events: MessageReader<GameNightEvent>,
    mut game: ResMut<Match>,
    mut menu: ResMut<Menu>,
    art: Res<Art>,
    mut images: ResMut<Assets<Image>>,
    mut materials: ResMut<Assets<ColorMaterial>>,
    balls: Query<(Entity, &Ball)>,
    stars: Query<Entity, Or<(With<Star>, With<Bomb>, With<Blast>)>>,
    mut music: Query<&mut AudioSink, With<Music>>,
) {
    // Pawns despawned earlier in this batch (Dispose then Prepare arrive together).
    let mut gone = Vec::new();
    for event in events.read() {
        match event {
            GameNightEvent::Prepare { seats, players, .. } => {
                // Load everything while hidden. New players can drop in mid-round.
                gn.participation(true);
                *menu = Menu::default();
                let rules = game.rules.clone();
                *game = Match { rules, ..default() };
                clear(&mut gone, &mut commands, &balls, &stars);
                spawn_balls(
                    &mut commands,
                    &gn,
                    seats,
                    players,
                    &art,
                    &mut images,
                    &mut materials,
                    &mut game,
                );
                new_round(&mut commands, &mut game, &art);
                game.started = true;
                gn.ready();
            }
            // The plugin shows the window and plays audio on Start and Resume,
            // and hides and pauses them on Pause. Simulation systems run only
            // while `gameplay_runs`, so there is nothing else to do here.
            GameNightEvent::Start { .. }
            | GameNightEvent::Pause { .. }
            | GameNightEvent::Resume { .. } => {}
            GameNightEvent::Dispose { .. } => {
                clear(&mut gone, &mut commands, &balls, &stars);
                game.started = false;
            }
            GameNightEvent::RosterChanged { seats, players, .. } => {
                // Keep the match going: add newcomers, drop pawns of those who left.
                let mut known = Vec::new();
                let alive: Vec<(Entity, &Ball)> =
                    balls.iter().filter(|(e, _)| !gone.contains(e)).collect();
                for (entity, ball) in alive {
                    let still = seats
                        .iter()
                        .any(|s| s.index == ball.seat && s.occupant.player_id() == ball.player);
                    if still {
                        known.push(ball.seat);
                    } else {
                        commands.entity(entity).try_despawn();
                        gone.push(entity);
                    }
                }
                let fresh: Vec<Seat> = seats
                    .iter()
                    .filter(|s| !known.contains(&s.index))
                    .cloned()
                    .collect();
                spawn_balls(
                    &mut commands,
                    &gn,
                    &fresh,
                    players,
                    &art,
                    &mut images,
                    &mut materials,
                    &mut game,
                );
            }
            GameNightEvent::PlayersUpdated { players } => {
                // A new name, colour or face for the same player: repaint, never restart.
                for (entity, ball) in balls.iter().filter(|(e, _)| !gone.contains(e)) {
                    if let Some(player) = players.iter().find(|p| Some(p.id) == ball.player) {
                        commands.entity(entity).despawn_children();
                        dress(
                            &mut commands,
                            entity,
                            Some(player),
                            ball.seat,
                            &gn,
                            &art,
                            &mut images,
                            &mut materials,
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
            GameNightEvent::SettingChanged { key, value } => {
                game.rules.apply(key, value);
            }
            GameNightEvent::PlayerSettings { player_id, .. } => {
                for (entity, ball) in balls.iter().filter(|(e, _)| !gone.contains(e)) {
                    if ball.player == Some(*player_id) {
                        commands.entity(entity).despawn_children();
                        let player = gn.player(*player_id).cloned();
                        dress(
                            &mut commands,
                            entity,
                            player.as_ref(),
                            ball.seat,
                            &gn,
                            &art,
                            &mut images,
                            &mut materials,
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
            GameNightEvent::ActionTriggered { key, player_id } if key == "new_round" => {
                let who = gn
                    .player(*player_id)
                    .map_or("Someone".into(), |p| p.name.clone());
                info!("{who} asked for a new round");
                new_round(&mut commands, &mut game, &art);
            }
            GameNightEvent::CompanionMessage { player_id, data } => {
                if data.get("action").and_then(|a| a.as_str()) == Some("dash") {
                    for (entity, ball) in balls.iter().filter(|(e, _)| !gone.contains(e)) {
                        if ball.player == Some(*player_id) {
                            commands
                                .entity(entity)
                                .entry::<Ball>()
                                .and_modify(|mut b| b.phone_dash = true);
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
            GameNightEvent::CompanionPresence {
                player_id,
                connected: true,
            } => {
                let view = phone_view(&gn, &game, *player_id);
                gn.companion_message(Some(*player_id), view);
            }
            GameNightEvent::GameCommand { id, text, .. } => {
                let (ok, answer) = command(&mut gn, text);
                gn.command_result(id.clone(), ok, answer);
            }
            GameNightEvent::HostMusic { playing } => {
                if let Ok(mut sink) = music.single_mut() {
                    sink.set_volume(Volume::Linear(if *playing { 0.0 } else { 0.35 }));
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

Source: sdk/bevy/demo/src/main.rs

Prepare can follow a Dispose in the same frame (a replay, a skip). Despawn with try_despawn and skip entities you already removed in the same batch.

Read each seat's controller

gn.pad(seat) returns the seat's controller for this frame: neutral when the seat has none, when input is more than 250 ms old and while the game is not running. stick applies a radial deadzone (up is positive y, as in Bevy's world), trigger a trigger deadzone. just_pressed is true once per press, and a button still held from the lobby has to be released before it counts. Never use Bevy's gamepad order under GameNight: a seat's controller is a host token.

fn steer(
    gn: Res<GameNight>,
    mut game: ResMut<Match>,
    mut balls: Query<&mut Ball>,
    time: Res<Time>,
) {
    let dt = time.delta_secs();
    game.present = balls.iter().map(|b| b.seat).collect();
    for mut ball in &mut balls {
        ball.dash = (ball.dash - dt).max(-0.6);
        ball.stunned = (ball.stunned - dt).max(0.0);
        if ball.bot || ball.stunned > 0.0 {
            continue;
        }
        let pad = gn.pad(ball.seat);
        let target = pad.stick(0)
            + Vec2::new(
                pad.pressed(PadButton::Right) as i32 as f32
                    - pad.pressed(PadButton::Left) as i32 as f32,
                pad.pressed(PadButton::Up) as i32 as f32
                    - pad.pressed(PadButton::Down) as i32 as f32,
            );
        let target = target.clamp_length_max(1.0) * SPEED;
        ball.velocity = ball.velocity.lerp(target, (dt * 12.0).min(1.0));
        let dash = pad.just_pressed(PadButton::A) || std::mem::take(&mut ball.phone_dash);
        if dash && ball.dash <= -0.6 {
            let dir = if target != Vec2::ZERO {
                target.normalize()
            } else {
                ball.velocity.normalize_or(Vec2::X)
            };
            ball.velocity = dir * DASH_SPEED;
            ball.dash = 0.18;
        }
    }
}

Source: sdk/bevy/demo/src/main.rs

AI seats get bots, empty seats get nothing. rumble(seat, weak, strong, seconds) vibrates a pad; standalone it drives the local gamepad.

Declare settings, phone buttons and a phone screen

Declare once at startup; the plugin declares again after each reconnect, and GameNight replays the values the party picked. A player scope gives every player a value of their own, which arrives as PlayerSettings.

fn settings() -> Vec<SettingSpec> {
    vec![
        SettingSpec {
            key: "round_seconds".into(),
            label: "Round length (next round)".into(),
            description: Some("Seconds per round.".into()),
            kind: SettingKind::Number {
                default: 60,
                min: 20,
                max: 180,
            },
            scope: SettingScope::Party,
        },
        SettingSpec {
            key: "stars".into(),
            label: "Stars".into(),
            description: None,
            kind: SettingKind::Choice {
                default: "normal".into(),
                options: vec!["few".into(), "normal".into(), "lots".into()],
            },
            scope: SettingScope::Party,
        },
        SettingSpec {
            key: "bombs".into(),
            label: "Bombs".into(),
            description: Some("Bombs flash, then knock stars out of everyone nearby.".into()),
            kind: SettingKind::Toggle { default: true },
            scope: SettingScope::Party,
        },
        SettingSpec {
            key: "shape".into(),
            label: "My shape".into(),
            description: Some("Every player picks their own.".into()),
            kind: SettingKind::Choice {
                default: "round".into(),
                options: vec!["round".into(), "square".into()],
            },
            scope: SettingScope::Player,
        },
    ]
}

Source: sdk/bevy/demo/src/main.rs

/// Declare once; the plugin declares again after a reconnect.
fn declare(mut gn: ResMut<GameNight>) {
    gn.declare_settings(settings());
    gn.declare_actions(vec![GameAction {
        key: "new_round".into(),
        label: "New round".into(),
        description: Some("Ends this round for everyone.".into()),
        confirm: true,
    }]);
    gn.declare_companion_folder("phone", "index.html");
    gn.declare_commands(
        "Change the round length, the number of stars or bombs.",
        vec![
            "90 second rounds".into(),
            "lots of stars".into(),
            "no bombs".into(),
        ],
    );
}

Source: sdk/bevy/demo/src/main.rs

declare_companion_folder looks for a relative folder next to the executable, under BEVY_ASSET_ROOT or CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, then the working directory. Ship the folder with your build. The page loads /assets/companion.js; see Phone screens and the demo's phone page.

Plain-text requests from the GameNight app or the session assistant arrive as GameCommand. Answer every one with command_result:

fn command(gn: &mut GameNight, text: &str) -> (bool, String) {
    let text = text.to_lowercase();
    if let Some(n) = text
        .split(|c: char| !c.is_ascii_digit())
        .find_map(|w| w.parse::<i64>().ok())
    {
        let n = n.clamp(20, 180);
        gn.set_setting("round_seconds", SettingValue::Number(n));
        return (
            true,
            format!("Rounds last {n} seconds from the next round."),
        );
    }
    for (word, value) in [
        ("few", "few"),
        ("less", "few"),
        ("lots", "lots"),
        ("more", "lots"),
        ("normal", "normal"),
    ] {
        if text.contains(word) && text.contains("star") {
            gn.set_setting("stars", SettingValue::Choice(value.into()));
            return (true, format!("Stars: {value}."));
        }
    }
    if text.contains("bomb") {
        let on = !(text.contains("no ") || text.contains("off") || text.contains("geen"));
        gn.set_setting("bombs", SettingValue::Toggle(on));
        return (true, format!("Bombs {}.", if on { "on" } else { "off" }));
    }
    (
        false,
        "I can change the round length, the stars and the bombs.".into(),
    )
}

The Start menu

Start opens your own menu, for everyone; Back belongs to GameNight. The game's name heads the menu, then Resume, then New round, then the settings, without button hints. The menu changes settings through set_setting, so the change also shows in the apps and comes back as SettingChanged (standalone too).

/// Start opens and closes the menu for everyone; any player can use it.
/// Back is never read: it belongs to GameNight.
fn menu_input(
    mut commands: Commands,
    mut gn: ResMut<GameNight>,
    mut menu: ResMut<Menu>,
    mut game: ResMut<Match>,
    art: Res<Art>,
) {
    if !gn.is_running() {
        return;
    }
    let seats: Vec<u8> = gn.seats.iter().map(|s| s.index).collect();
    for seat in seats {
        let pad = gn.pad(seat);
        if pad.just_pressed(PadButton::Start) {
            menu.open = !menu.open;
            menu.row = 0;
            continue;
        }
        if !menu.open {
            continue;
        }
        let vertical =
            pad.just_pressed(PadButton::Down) as i32 - pad.just_pressed(PadButton::Up) as i32;
        menu.row = (menu.row as i32 + vertical).rem_euclid(MENU_ROWS.len() as i32) as usize;
        let step =
            pad.just_pressed(PadButton::Right) as i64 - pad.just_pressed(PadButton::Left) as i64;
        let row = MENU_ROWS[menu.row];
        match row {
            "Resume" if pad.just_pressed(PadButton::A) || pad.just_pressed(PadButton::B) => {
                menu.open = false
            }
            "New round" if pad.just_pressed(PadButton::A) => {
                menu.open = false;
                new_round(&mut commands, &mut game, &art);
            }
            "Resume" | "New round" => {
                if pad.just_pressed(PadButton::B) {
                    menu.open = false;
                }
            }
            key => {
                let step = if pad.just_pressed(PadButton::A) && step == 0 {
                    1
                } else {
                    step
                };
                if step != 0 {
                    let next = next_value(key, &game.rules.value(key), step);
                    // Through GameNight, so the apps show the same value.
                    gn.set_setting(key, next);
                }
                if pad.just_pressed(PadButton::B) {
                    menu.open = false;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

Source: sdk/bevy/demo/src/main.rs

Rounds keep going

At the end of a round, show the result briefly, put the winner in the room log, save each player's progress and call finished(). Then start the next round yourself: finished() does not end the session. Players leave with Back.

fn round_clock(
    mut commands: Commands,
    mut gn: ResMut<GameNight>,
    mut game: ResMut<Match>,
    art: Res<Art>,
    time: Res<Time>,
) {
    let dt = time.delta_secs();
    if game.in_results() {
        game.results -= dt;
        if game.results <= 0.0 {
            new_round(&mut commands, &mut game, &art);
        }
        return;
    }
    game.clock -= dt;
    if game.clock > 0.0 {
        return;
    }
    // Round over: show the result, tell GameNight, save stats, go again.
    game.clock = 0.0;
    game.results = RESULTS_SECONDS;
    let best = game.scores.iter().max_by_key(|e| e.stars).copied();
    if let Some(best) = best.filter(|e| e.stars > 0) {
        let name = best
            .player
            .and_then(|id| gn.player(id))
            .map_or("A bot".into(), |p| p.name.clone());
        gn.room_log(format!(
            "{name} wins round {} with {} stars",
            game.round, best.stars
        ));
    }
    // Lifetime stars and wins follow each profile to the next game night.
    for entry in game.scores.clone() {
        let Some(id) = entry.player else { continue };
        let old = gn.player_data(id).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| json!({}));
        let total = old.get("stars").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0) + entry.stars as u64;
        let won = best.is_some_and(|b| b.player == Some(id) && b.stars > 0);
        let wins = old.get("wins").and_then(|v| v.as_u64()).unwrap_or(0) + u64::from(won);
        gn.save_player_data(id, json!({ "stars": total, "wins": wins }));
    }
    gn.finished();
}

Source: sdk/bevy/demo/src/main.rs

save_player_data keeps up to 64 KB of JSON with a player's profile between nights; player_data reads it back. Guests keep it for the night only.

Faces, colours and couch order

avatar_image(player) decodes a player's drawn face into a nearest-filtered Image plus where the head sits in it. Draw a circle in the skin colour and put the drawing's head centre on it. hex_color reads profile colours.

/// The body in the player's colour, a head in their skin colour and their face.
fn dress(
    commands: &mut Commands,
    entity: Entity,
    player: Option<&Player>,
    seat: u8,
    gn: &GameNight,
    art: &Art,
    images: &mut Assets<Image>,
    materials: &mut Assets<ColorMaterial>,
) {
    let fallback = bot_color(seat);
    let color = hex_color(player.and_then(|p| p.color.as_deref()), fallback);
    let skin = hex_color(
        player.and_then(|p| p.skin_color.as_deref()),
        Color::srgb(0.96, 0.8, 0.66),
    );
    let square = player
        .and_then(|p| gn.player_setting(p.id, "shape"))
        .is_some_and(|v| v == SettingValue::Choice("square".into()));
    let body = if square {
        art.square.clone()
    } else {
        art.circle.clone()
    };
    commands.entity(entity).with_children(|parent| {
        parent.spawn((
            Body,
            Mesh2d(body),
            MeshMaterial2d(materials.add(color)),
            Transform::from_scale(Vec3::splat(BODY)),
        ));
        parent.spawn((
            Mesh2d(art.circle.clone()),
            MeshMaterial2d(materials.add(skin)),
            Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 4.0, 0.1).with_scale(Vec3::splat(HEAD)),
        ));
        match player.and_then(avatar_image) {
            Some((image, head)) => {
                // Put the head centre of the drawing on the head circle.
                let scale = HEAD / head.radius;
                let size = Vec2::new(image.width() as f32, image.height() as f32);
                let offset = (size / 2.0 - Vec2::from(head.center)) * Vec2::new(1.0, -1.0) * scale;
                parent.spawn((
                    Face,
                    Sprite {
                        image: images.add(image),
                        custom_size: Some(size * scale),
                        ..default()
                    },
                    Transform::from_xyz(offset.x, 4.0 + offset.y, 0.2),
                ));
            }
            None => {
                for x in [-7.0, 7.0] {
                    parent.spawn((
                        Mesh2d(art.circle.clone()),
                        MeshMaterial2d(art.dark.clone()),
                        Transform::from_xyz(x, 7.0, 0.2).with_scale(Vec3::splat(3.2)),
                    ));
                }
            }
        }
    });
}

Source: sdk/bevy/demo/src/main.rs

Lay anything that runs left to right out with couch_order(seats, players): the order in which players sit, which they choose in the lobby. Call it again when players update, because people move mid-match.

Host music

When the host plays music, GameNightEvent::HostMusic { playing: true } arrives and host_music_playing() is true. Mute your music, not your effects, and turn it back up when it stops.

Run and test

cd sdk/bevy
cargo run -p bevy-demo                      # standalone: keyboard and gamepads
cargo run -p bevy-demo -- --bots 3          # with three bots
cargo run -p bevy-demo -- --bots 3 --shot star-catch.png
xvfb-run -a cargo test --workspace          # plugin tests and the conformance harness

To play it through a development host, start the host and set GAMENIGHT_ADDR=127.0.0.1:7912 before running the demo. For your own game, run the harness the same way, with your game id and binary:

cargo run -p gamenight-certify -- my-game --players 2 -- path/to/my-game

What is not covered yet

These were checked on Linux (X11, software rendering) with synthetic controller frames. Windows and macOS window behaviour, the Windows foreground-permission helper the Godot SDK uses on Pause, physical controllers and real audio devices still need testing on hardware. The plugin hides the window rather than minimising it; Alt-Tab back to a paused game goes through the lobby. See Engine support for how this compares with the other engines.
